summary: Duplin County, NC steel tower that a state lookout history dates to 1935 (CCC-built); 1969 survey gives 110 ft; no source describes it today.

facts.design: Steel tower with a metal cabin
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Civilian Conservation Corps erected a 99-foot 9-inch steel tower; the history gives costs of $1,630.04 funded through the Emergency Conservation Works program.
CCC Camp P-68 completed a five-room frame house as living quarters for the lookout.
The lease on the property expired and the State purchased the property that summer.
Coast and Geodetic Survey first observed and described the station: metal cabin on a four-legged steel skeleton structure, 110 feet high.
Survey station recovery note by US Power Squadron: recovered in good condition.

notes_for_editor: Built date, cost, agency and the 1961 land purchase rest on one compiled history page (Forest Lookouts), which cites state biennial reports but was not checked against them. Height conflict is unresolved: the 1935 steel tower is 99 ft 9 in per the history; the 1969 survey describes a 110 ft structure. Story gives both and says the sources do not explain the gap. No source found describes the site or the tower today. Latest condition note is the 1986 survey recovery. Brief status and access stay unknown and are not set in facts. Web search budget was exhausted during this run, so no search was done; only cached pages and direct page reads were used. The 1969 directions are historical and not confirmed.
